text: 11. Health Sciences: Pharmacy, CSR, and Procedures

This chapter covers the three health sciences / supply chain modules: Pharmacy (medication management), CSR (Clinical Service Request - medical supplies and equipment), and Procedures (clinical procedures and services). All three share a common order-and-dispense pattern: master data -> order from OPD/ER/inpatient -> items created -> dispensing -> patient medication/supply record -> billing.

Route prefix: /pharmacy. Manages pharmaceutical services: drug master data, drug batch/lot tracking, inventory management, purchase orders, stock adjustments, dispensing to patients, patient medication records (PMR), pharmacy reports, and printing pharmacy requests.

Route: pharmacy.drugs (permission: pharmacy.manage). Drug/product catalog. Fields: id, drug_name, generic_name, brand_name, drug_category, drug_form (tablet/capsule/syrup/injection/etc.), strength (e.g. 500mg), route (PO/oral, IV, IM, SC, topical, etc.), unit_of_measure (tablet, ml, vial, ampule, box, etc.), standard_charge (float), is_generic (bool), is_controlled (bool - controlled substance requiring extra tracking), supplier_id (FK to supply_suppliers, nullable), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. Drugs are ordered via PharmacyRequest from OPD/ER/inpatient.

Route: pharmacy.drug-batches (permission: pharmacy.manage). Drug batch/lot tracking for inventory management and expiry control. Critical for drug safety (recalls, expiry dating). Fields: id, drug_id (FK to pharmacy_drugs), batch_number, manufacturer, manufacturing_date, expiry_date (critical for expiry alerts), quantity_received, quantity_dispensed, quantity_on_hand, unit_cost, supplier_id, received_date, received_by, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. When a drug is dispensed, the batch quantity is decremented. Expired or near-expiry batches are flagged.

Route: pharmacy.inventory (permission: pharmacy.manage). Current inventory position for each drug. Aggregates/display the on-hand quantity across all batches, or a snapshot table. Fields: id, drug_id (FK), total_quantity_on_hand, total_quantity_dispensed, last_count_date, last_counted_by, reorder_level (min stock alert), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. Inventory shows the drug's current availability for dispensing.

Route: pharmacy.purchase-orders (permission: pharmacy.manage). Purchase orders to suppliers for drug procurement. Fields: id, po_number (e.g. PO-00001), supplier_id (FK to supply_suppliers), order_date, expected_delivery_date, status (Pending/Ordered/Partially Received/Received/Cancelled), notes, total_amount, created_by, created_date, updated_by, updated_date, history. Each PO has PO items (PharmacyPurchaseOrderItem): drug_id, batch_number (if specific), quantity_ordered, unit_cost, quantity_received, line_total, is_active, history.

Route: pharmacy.stock-adjustments (permission: pharmacy.manage). Inventory adjustments: corrections, damages, losses, returns, returns-to-vendor, donations, stock counts. Fields: id, adjustment_no, drug_id (FK), batch_id (FK, nullable - can adjust specific batch or aggregate), adjustment_type (Stock In, Stock Out, Damage/Loss, Return to Vendor, Correction, Physical Count Adjustment, Expiration Write-off), quantity_before, quantity_after, quantity_adjusted, reason, adjusted_by, adjustment_date, notes, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

items: id - Primary key.
tenant_id - FK to hospitals.id.
pharmacy_request_code - Code: 'PR-' + 5-digit sequence (e.g. PR-00001).
opd_consultation_id / er_admission_id / admission_id - Context FKs (one of these is set depending on where the order originated).
patient_id - FK to patients.id.
requesting_department_id - FK to departments.id.
requesting_person - String. Name of person requesting.
requesting_doctor_id - FK to health_care_professionals.id.
priority - String: Stat, Urgent, Routine. Default 'Routine'.
status - Request status: Pending, In Progress, Dispensed, Partially Dispensed, Cancelled.
notes - Text (nullable).
created_by / created_date - Audit columns.
updated_by / updated_date - Audit columns.
history - Soft delete flag (1=active).
is_active - Active flag.
id - Primary key.
pharmacy_request_id - FK to pharmacy_requests.id.
drug_id - FK to pharmacy_drugs.id.
drug_name - String. Denormalized drug name.
generic_name - String. Denormalized generic name.
drug_form - String. Denormalized form.
strength - String. Denormalized strength.
route - String. Denormalized route.
quantity - Float. Quantity ordered (default 1, can be any).

frequency - String (nullable). Dosage frequency: OD (once daily), BID (twice daily), TID (three times daily), QID (four times daily), q4h, q6h, q8h, q12h, STAT, etc. Set per-drug in the order modal (orderPharmacyFrequencies[$drugId]).
route_admin - String (nullable). Route of administration: PO, IV, IM, SC, SL, Inhalation, Topical, etc. Set per-drug in the order modal (orderPharmacyRoutes[$drugId]).
duration - String (nullable). Duration of therapy (e.g. '5 days', '3 weeks').
dose_instructions - Text (nullable). Special dosing instructions.
charge_amount - Float. Drug's standard_charge.
batch_id - FK to pharmacy_drug_batches.id (nullable). The specific batch dispensed from (set during dispensing).
batch_number - String (nullable). Denormalized batch number.
expiry_date - Date (nullable). Batch expiry (set during dispensing).
is_dispensed - Boolean. Whether this item has been dispensed.
dispensed_quantity - Float (nullable). Quantity actually dispensed (may be less than ordered if stock insufficient).
dispensed_by - FK to users (nullable).
dispensed_date - DateTime (nullable).
created_by / created_date - Audit columns.
updated_by / updated_date - Audit columns.
history - Soft delete flag (1=active).
is_active - Active flag.

text: From OPD (placePharmacyOrder), ER (see 7.6), or directly. Summary:

items: Doctor/nurse selects drugs from the pharmacy catalog.
For each drug: quantity (default 1), frequency (orderPharmacyFrequencies[$drugId]), route (orderPharmacyRoutes[$drugId]) set per-drug.
PharmacyRequest created with request_code = 'PR-' + 5-digit sequence, status = 'Pending'.
PharmacyRequestItems created for each drug with drug details, quantity, frequency, route, charge_amount.
Founded drugs can optionally be linked to a batch at order time or at dispense time.
The request appears in Pharmacy > Dispensing for the pharmacist to process.
Pharmacist reviews the pending PharmacyRequest and its items.
For each item: selects the batch to dispense from (batch_id), verifies expiry date, enters dispensed_quantity (may be less than ordered if stock unavailable - partial dispense).
When all items are dispensed: status becomes 'Dispensed'. If only some items dispensed: 'Partially Dispensed'.
dispensed_by and dispensed_date are set for each item.
Batch quantities are decremented (quantity_dispensed incremented, quantity_on_hand decremented).
The patient's medication record (PMR) is updated (see 11.1.3).

text: Route: pharmacy.pmr (permission: pharmacy.view). The PMR shows ALL medications a patient has been prescribed and dispensed across all encounters (OPD, ER, inpatient). This is the patient's medication history.

items: View by patient: select patient, see all medication orders (pharmacy requests) with their items, frequencies, routes, dates, and dispensing status.

Each medication entry shows: drug name, generic name, form, strength, route, frequency, quantity, duration, start date, end date (computed from frequency x duration), dispensing status, prescribing doctor.
The PMR is used for medication reconciliation (checking for drug interactions, allergies, duplicate therapy).
PMR is the pharmacy counterpart to the patient chart's medication history.

text: Route: pharmacy.reports (permission: pharmacy.reports). Pharmacy reports: drug dispensing report (by drug, by period), inventory status report, expiry report (drugs expiring within X days), purchase order status report, top selling drugs, stock adjustment report.

items: pharmacy.request.print ({pharmacyRequest}) - Prints the pharmacy request/form with all items, quantities, frequencies, routes, charges. Used by pharmacist as dispensing worksheet.
pharmacy.request.encounter-print ({opdConsultationId}) - Prints all pharmacy requests for a given OPD encounter on one page. Consolidated dispensing list for the encounter.

text: Route prefix: /supply. The CSR module manages medical supplies, equipment, and non-pharmaceutical consumables. 'CSR' stands for Clinical Service Request - the supply chain module that handles issuance of medical supplies to patients/departments. Pattern identical to pharmacy: master data -> order -> dispense -> record -> print.

items: Supply > Units (supply.units) - Units of measure: pcs, box, pack, set, roll, sheet, pair, each, etc.

Supply > Categories (supply.categories) - Supply categories: Surgical Supplies, Dressing & Wound Care, IV Therapy Supplies, Syringes & Needles, PPE (Gloves, Masks, Gowns, Goggles), Respiratory Supplies, Patient Care Supplies, Linen & Textiles, Office/Non-Medical, etc.
Supply > Suppliers (supply.suppliers) - Supplier/vendor details: name, contact, address, email, phone, tax_id, is_active.

Supply > Stock Locations (supply.stock-locations) - Physical storage locations: Pharmacy Store, ER Supply Room, Ward 1 Supply, Central Supply, ICU Supply, OR Supply, etc. Fields: id, name, code, description, floor, is_active.

Supply > Items (supply.items) - Supply item catalog: item_name, generic_name, category_id, unit_id, standard_charge, stock_location_id, reorder_level, is_active. Fields: id, item_name, generic_name, category_id (FK), unit_id (FK), standard_charge (float), stock_location_id (FK to supply_stock_locations), reorder_level (int), is_active, tenant_id, history.
Supply > Inventory (supply.inventory) - Current stock per item per location: item_id, stock_location_id, quantity_on_hand, quantity_dispensed, last_count_date, last_counted_by, is_active.

Supply > Stock Adjustments (supply.stock-adjustments) - Same pattern as pharmacy: item_id, stock_location_id, adjustment_type, quantity, reason, adjusted_by, adjustment_date, notes. For stock corrections, damages, expirations, returns.

CsrRequest: Code 'CR-' + 5-digit sequence. Same context pattern: opd_consultation_id, er_admission_id, admission_id, patient_id, requesting_department_id, requesting_person, priority (default 'Routine'), status (Pending/In Progress/Dispensed/Partially Dispensed/Cancelled), notes, audit columns.

CsrRequestItem: csr_request_id, item_id (FK to supply_items), item_name, category, unit, quantity (orderCsrQuantities[$itemId]), notes, charge_amount, is_dispensed, dispensed_quantity, dispensed_by, dispensed_date, batch/lot info (if applicable).
Order flow (placeCsrOrder): doctor/nurse selects items, quantities set per-item, request + items created with 'CR-' code, status 'Pending'.

Dispense flow: CSR/warehouse officer reviews request, dispenses quantities from stock location inventory, decrements inventory, marks items as dispensed, advances status to 'Dispensed' or 'Partially Dispensed'.
CSR items don't have frequency/route (unlike pharmacy) - they are consumable supplies.
supply.request.print ({csrRequest}) - Prints CSR request/form with items, quantities, charges.
supply.request.encounter-print ({opdConsultationId}) - Consolidated CSR requests for an encounter.

text: Route prefix: /procedures. Manages clinical procedures/services: procedure categories and procedures catalog, ordering, and dispensing of procedural services.

items: Procedures > Categories (procedures.categories) - Procedure categories: Surgical, Medical, Diagnostic, Therapeutic, Obstetric, Anesthesia, Endoscopy, Cardiac Catheterization, Hemodialysis, etc. Fields: id, name, code, description, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

Procedures > Procedures (procedures.procedures) - Procedure catalog. Each procedure: name, code, category_id (FK), description, standard_charge (float), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. Examples: Incision & Drainage, Suture Removal, Wound Debridement, Cast Application, ECG (12-lead), Nebulization, IV Cannulation, Urinary Catheterization, Foley Catheterization, Blood Transfusion (Packed RBC), Oxygen Therapy, Nebulization with Salbutamol, etc.
Procedures are ordered via ProcedureRequest from OPD/ER/inpatient and dispensed when performed.

ProcedureRequest: Code 'Proc-' + 5-digit sequence. Same context pattern (opd_consultation_id, er_admission_id, admission_id, patient_id, requesting_department_id, requesting_person, priority, status).

ProcedureRequestItem: procedure_request_id, procedure_id (FK to procedures_procedures), procedure_name, category, standard_charge, quantity (orderProcedureQuantities[$procedureId] - usually 1 for procedures), notes, is_dispensed (performed), dispensed_by, dispensed_date, duration (minutes, if applicable).
Order flow (placeProcedureOrder): doctor selects procedures, quantities set per-procedure, request + items created with 'Proc-' code, status 'Pending'.
Dispense flow: procedure is performed (nurse/therapist/technician performs it), items marked as dispensed (is_dispensed=true), dispensed_by/dispensed_date set, status advances.
Procedure orders integrate with billing (charge_amount flows to billing) and OR scheduling (for surgical procedures - can link to OR schedule).
There is no procedures.print route shown in the current page listing (only procedures categories and procedures CRUD + dispensing).
